title: The lang and xml:lang attributes must agree
summary: The html element has lang and xml:lang attributes with different languages. Make them match, or remove xml:lang if you do not need it.
problem: The <html> element has both lang and xml:lang attributes, and they name different base languages, for example lang="en" and xml:lang="fr". Software cannot tell which language is correct.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users, whose software may pick the wrong voice and pronunciation when the two values disagree. Translation tools can also guess wrongly.
whyItMatters: Conflicting language information makes the page read out in a voice that does not match the text. It falls under WCAG 3.1.1 at Level A, the baseline that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Find the opening <html> tag and read both attributes.
Decide which language the page is written in.
Set lang and xml:lang to the same language code, or remove xml:lang. It is only needed for pages served as XML (XHTML).
Check any template that prints both attributes, so every page gets matching values.
